newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currency futures end spotty trade higher.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currency futures end spotty trade higher.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended mostly higher after a session characterized by patchy trading activity.
Yen slumped further late on selling that again accelerated as the December futures entered the $0.008950 area on its trek to yet another new contract low, this at $0.008948.
Traders said yen's outlook remained bearish technically and fundamentally, with this weekend's Japanese general election not expected to alter that perception.
"Yen closed very weak," said one floor broker in currency futures. "I'm looking for 113.00 next week."
That would equate to a fall in December yen futures to about $0.008920.
Swiss francs also fell to another new contract low Friday, pressured partly by signs that the Russian tensions that had heated up on Thursday were abating.
Indeed, brokers said currencies on Friday showed muted response when Russian president Boris Yeltsin dismissed his armed forces chief of staff, General Mikhail Kolesnikov.
Some brokers said they saw signs that dealers were shifting their safe-haven funds out of the Swiss unit and into Sterling, which also was expected to continue moving upward.
Sterling jumped before midday to another new contract high, lifted by ideas that U.K. rates have room to rise.

A British newspaper Friday quoted Tim Congdon, a member of the so-called "Wise Men" panel, as saying he favored a one percentage point increase in official U.K. rates to avert need for more drastic measures later.
Futures briefly firmed after the August U.S. trade gap shrank 6.6 percent to $10.83 billion from July's revised $11.60 billion, wider than the $8.5 billion gap forecast.
Yen had dipped overseas when Japan's September unadjusted customs-cleared trade surplus fell 30.3 percent vs a year ago.
The trend lower in Japan's trade surplus fueled ideas Japanese rates will stay low to encourage the recovery.

Yen ended off $0.000023 at $0.008957, marks firmed $0.0002 to $0.6506, Swiss frnacs fell $0.0006 to $0.7917, Sterling rose $0.0030 to $1.5882, Canadian dollar rose $0.0024 to $0.7442, Australian dollar rose $0.0028 to $0.7939, and Mexican peso ended flat at $0.124825. -Derivatives Desk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
